chosen: the 13 names are advertised once, in group 5, after every branch exists
why: per-group advertising pushes each task past its file limit and needs the generator twice per group; Kotlin's registry test checks both ways, so registrations land with the names

chosen: Wrap's line breaking and placement live in both cores (WrapRuns), tested on Linux/JVM
why: pure maths shared by both SDKs; the UI layouts only feed child sizes

chosen: the engine check 'each native vector gets the layout page whole' is red from G4 to G5
why: the demo page lands in G4 so the hand checks can follow G5; the names go out in G5

chosen: native Baseline ideographic draws as alphabetic, documented
options: measure an ideographic baseline from font metrics
why: SwiftUI and Compose expose only first and last text baselines; a font-metric baseline is new text-layout code for a rare case

chosen: D1 (demo page + engine test) starts during group 2
why: engine and example files only, no shared build tree; its expected red starts earlier and is reported at each gate until G5

chosen: keep: native Column children see a bounded height, so LimitedBox does not cap in a plain Column; Row/Column follow-up
why: both native SDKs bound a plain Column's children today; reading orcaFlexAxis is wrong behind a bounded box; unbounding every child is a Row/Column change outside step 3

chosen: the layout page's body sits in a SafeArea with every edge on
options: a no-op SafeArea with every edge off
why: draws the same on all three under an AppBar and keeps content above the home indicator; mid-page SafeAreas pad differently by design

chosen: the Offstage child holds a page-state counter and an unbound TextField
why: only typed text proves the child stayed mounted; a page-state counter survives a rebuild too

chosen: Kotlin: a baseline-aligned Row inside IntrinsicHeight takes its tallest child's height; follow-up
options: a separate baseline pass in the intrinsics
why: Compose intrinsics carry no baselines; the case is rare and a baseline pass is new measuring code outside the row's checks

chosen: Swift ConstrainedBox: the box keeps min and max; a child that hugs its content is not stretched to the min unless the axis is forced; documented, follow-up
options: a min-size environment every SDK widget reads
why: SwiftUI has no minimum constraint to pass down; a new environment read by every widget is a cross-cutting change outside step 3; the box's own size matches Flutter
